text: If you were born as Lucia Caminos, you'd learn to throw a punch before you learn to read.
You'd go to prison for the people you love and then you'd trust one man with your whole future.
Never sure if he's your way out or the end of the road.
But right now, you're a baby in a family that wants far more than it has.
Your mother comes from Liberty City and she carries one dream everywhere she goes.
The good life. A real one with money, safety and a front door that actually locks.
Keep that dream in mind. It decides everything later.
Your father gives you a different gift. The moment you can walk, he teaches you how to fight.
Fists up, chin down, hit first if you have to. It's not cruelty. In your house, it's love.
Because your family has always known the truth. The game is rigged against people like you
and nobody is coming to fix it. Years pass and the cute baby is gone.
You're sharp, stubborn and loyal to the point of pain. Life keeps swinging at you and you swing
back harder than you become a mother. A baby boy named Tommy. For the first time,
you're not just fighting for yourself. Then comes the worst day of your life.
A robbery at a payday loan store goes wrong. Alarms, sirens, a chase through the streets.
You left Tommy at a coffee shop and every second counts so you run straight back for him.
But someone has already reported a baby left alone. The police are waiting at the door,
handcuffs and your son is taken into child welfare custody.
Now you're in an orange jumpsuit inside a prison in Leonida staring at a concrete wall.
You want only two things. Get out and get Tommy back. A prison counselor asks about your
case and your chances of early release. You answer calmly like someone who has run out of tears.
Then the counselor mentions the name and your whole story turns.
Jason Duvall. Who is he? Your partner? While you sit behind bars, he's out in the keys,
running smuggling jobs for a man named Brian Heeder. He's not rich. He's not safe. But
he's the one person who makes a better life feel possible and you know you're that person
for him too. Then for once, luck is on your side. You're released early. Jason is waiting at the gate.
You celebrate at a little bar called the Rusty Anchor and he takes you home.
For one night, nobody is chasing you. Quick pause. If this story is pulling you in,
subscribe and drop a character name in the comments. The most like one gets born next.
The next morning, the clock starts ticking. You need money and you need it fast
because getting a son back costs more than courage. So you jump into Jason's smuggling
runs without a second thought. Late night drives, hidden cargo, risky deals. You're a natural.
Then a man named Mattia shows up with a pickup job that pays way too well. Jason smells a trap
and he says so. But you push. You've been poor your whole life. You've been locked up
and you're done waiting. You say yes. Remember that moment. It's the first domino.
It's a setup. Police arrest you both. Jason is badly wounded. Masked men and dirty cops attack
from every side and then they burn your home to the ground. Everything you just started building
gone in one night. You grab Jason and run bleeding and wanted to a small town in Kelly County.
Port Gellhorn. No money, no friends, no plan. And Jason is barely holding on.
So you become the one who holds everything together. You find supplies,
painkillers, local contacts. You make deals you'd never have made before. One leads to a kidnapping.
Another ends with someone dead. And Jason lives because of it. You tell yourself it was
worse it. But was it? Pills don't pay the rent. So you do the only thing you know.
You rob. Small stores first, then bigger ones. You're good at it. Scarily good. Still,
you know it won't last. Small robberies will never buy Tommy back. You need one huge score.
And the biggest city in Leonida is waiting. Vice city. Then hunters from the hospital find you.
No time to pack. You drag Jason out into the night, wounded, hunted, and carrying one thing
powerful people want back. A bag. And you still don't know what's inside it. The neon
skyline rises ahead. A fresh start, not even close. Because the people who built your trap
are still out there. In part two, vice city. A bank, a betrayal, and a bridge. Vice city hits you
like a slap. Neon lights, loud music, hot nights, and more money than you've ever seen.
And not a dollar of it is yours. So you and Jason start at the bottom. You take jobs for
a nightclub owner named Booby. And then you join the crew of a bank robber named Raul.
For the first time in months, things are working. Raul has a plan. The scene front at a national bank.
You and Jason are in. And when the chapter ends, the crew pulls it off. For one night,
you're rich, you're free. And you almost believe the good life your mother dreamed
about has finally arrived. Almost. Because cops don't forget faces. So you buy new names.
A lawyer named Abe Gonzalez builds you fake identities. And you start working for a woman
named Valentina. Jason takes a job at the airport, quietly collecting information.
And you? You walk into a gym and slip into the crew of a man named Cordell Grant. You smile,
you lift, you listen. Always listening. Then during an airport heist, Raul double crosses
Cordell. Bold, dangerous and not nearly smart enough. Because behind his back, Valentina sells
Raul to a dirty cop named Mendes. Raul's story ends in blood. One more friend gone and one more
lesson. In Vice City, loyalty lasts exactly until the price is right. And now the price is on you.
Abe makes you an offer. Give up Jason and your legal problems get much easier. A clean path.
A real shot at your son. It's the easiest way out of this nightmare you've ever been given.
You say no. No speech, no drama. Just no. But that night, you and Jason finally ask the
question you've both been avoiding. Should you even stay together? Because loving him might be
exactly why you never get free. Then a message arrives from Mattia, the man who started it
all. And it leads you to the real owner of the bag. Giorgio Gallo, calm, polite and terrifying.
Inside that bag was a hard drive. And he's using it to blackmail a senator named Camila Fuentes.
He doesn't punish you for taking it. He hires you. Cocaine smuggling. A war against the Albanian
mob. You steal a helicopter. You kidnap a sniffer dog. You blow up a rival shipment.
And people don't make it out alive. Vinny and Liz are killed along the way.
Every job gets deeper and every job feels more like a leash. Then Giorgio betrays you.
Police take you and Jason into custody. A prosecutor named Danica Howard tells you the
deal. You walk free. Only if you bring her that hard drive. The one thing Giorgio refuses
to give up. So you fight your way out. Dirty cops one after another. Mendes finds you
and you face him. Then you and Jason storm Giorgio's penthouse and take the drive.
You did it. And then you run out of road. A bridge. Police lights in every direction.
No way out. Jason says he'll surrender. He'll leave the drive with you so you
can take the deal and go home to Tommy. You look at him and you refuse. Because
you've never once given up on him. And now comes the choice. In one ending, Jason
convinces you to jump together, hand in hand, off the bridge. He slips the drive to you first.
Then in midair he lets go. You hit the water and escape. Jason is arrested. In the credits,
you take the prosecutor's deal and finally hold your son again. Years later,
you bring Tommy to visit his father in prison. In the other ending, you refuse to surrender.
You and Jason stand side by side and open fire. A final stand, just like Bonnie and Clyde.
You fall together, still holding hands. Tommy grows up without you and your mother visits him,
a photo of you and Jason sitting in a frame at home. And those are just two of the endings.
You started life with your fists up. You lost your freedom, your home and nearly your son.
You turned down an easy way out and you chose Jason every time it hurt. So tell me,
on that bridge, would you jump or would you stand and fight before you choose on that bridge?
There's something you need to know. The ending was never decided there. It was decided
a hundred small moments ago and you barely noticed. Every job you took with Jason made
your bond stronger or weaker. The game counts it heart by heart. At the very top,
it's a bond meant to last through life and death. Every robbery and every shootout was
counted too. Are you a clean, careful professional? Or someone wild, loud and out of control?
The game decides who you are and it remembers. Then there's money. Not the thrill of cash,
but a quiet savings account on your phone. Inside an app called Bug Me, the goal starts
small, $5,000. Then $15,000. Then $100,000. Every dollar you save is a promise to Tommy.
There's even a side quest where you send money to Lucia's aunt,
so she can look after your boy while you're out there breaking the law.
Skip it and some doors close for good. Even mercy comes back around. Early in the story,
Jason spares a man named Arnold. Months later, Brian makes peace with him and sends you $10,000.
One small kindness paid back when you need it most. So when you reach the bridge,
the game already knows exactly who you are. Police lights on both sides.
Two doors. Swim for it or never surrender. Choose to jump, and your love is strong,
and your record is careful, but your savings fall short. Jason points toward the sand bank and says,
we jump. In midair, he lets go of your hand, so you land free.
He's arrested. He spends the rest of his life in prison with one last visit from his son,
and you raise Tommy alone. Now the same jump, the same sacrifice,
but this time you saved every dollar. And suddenly money talks. You call Abe,
the lawyer who once offered you a way out at Jason's expense. This time you use him to bring
Jason home. Through cash and some very shady deals, a prison door opens. In the final scene,
the family sits together. It's the happiest ending in the whole game.
Now choose to never surrender. You and Jason charge the police guns drawn.
A bloody shootout. You fall together. Tommy is raised by your aunt and your mother, Mia,
who will have to explain the one thing a child should never have to hear.
And then there's the darkest door. If you've played too wild,
if the game has decided you're a psychopath, even the jump can't save you.
Jason suggests it. You kiss. Then he steps out of the car with his hands raised, ready
to surrender. The police shoot first. You both die instantly. Tommy grows up with his aunt,
and Mia visits him in tears. Four endings, and Rockstar says there are more.
None of them is bad, only different. When the credits finally end, the game doesn't let go.
You're back in Vice City. The finale still marked on the map. The game asks if you're ready,
and for Jason and Lucia, the answer is not yet. They drive back into the Neon.
You can finish the map, chase 100%, or return to that bridge and try again.
Think about where this started. A baby taught to fight before she could walk.
A mother who dreamed of a better life. A robbery, a prison cell, a son taken away.
You turned down the easy way out. You chose Jason, even when it hurt.
And in the end, everything came down to who you became and what you saved along the way.
So tell me, on that bridge, which door would you choose?
